A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same LEAD/TFv6 study and support comparison of their text, figures, tables, and mathematical content. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; supplementary material referenced in the text is unavailable and is not assessed.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 report original CARLA experiments, ablations, inference-time measurements, and transfer results on NAVSIM and WOD-E2E.

after.justification: Sections 3–4 retain original CARLA experiments and ablations, together with NAVSIM and WOD-E2E transfer results.

M1.justification: The expert-alignment rules, GRU removal, three-target conditioning, radar integration, and LTFv6 adaptation remain unchanged. The new architecture diagram in Figure 3 documents the existing method rather than establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LEAD training coverage and evaluate Bench2Drive, Longest6 v2, Town13 validation/training scenarios, NAVSIM v1/v2, and WOD-E2E. No driving dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Removing v1 Table 6 and its discussion removes the latency comparisons against TFv5 with two backbones and the reported comparison with SimLingo. Comparator membership in the retained driving-performance experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 removes the separate per-frame inference-timing evaluation on a single RTX 2080 Ti. Retained driving splits, metrics, training budgets, and model configurations are unchanged. Replacing camera counts with field-of-view descriptions does not establish an actual sensor-setting change.

E4.justification: The inference-efficiency analysis is removed, and Figure 2 revises the diagnostic evidence for TFv5 vehicle-blocked and stop infractions. The state-alignment, GRU, target-point, sensor/backbone, and Town13 generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports uncertainty values and describes Town13 results as means over three evaluations of each agent. V2 explicitly describes averaging three independently trained models with different seeds across Sections 3–4 and table captions; Section 3.1 specifies one evaluation per model. This clarifies replication without establishing that additional runs occurred.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes TFv6 Town13 validation IS from 0.28 to 0.30 and DS from 2.65 to 3.52, and training DS from 5.01 to 5.28; NDS remains unchanged. Figure 2 changes TFv5 blocked infractions from approximately 77 to 27 and stop infractions from approximately 5 to 18 per 100 km. The latency results and highway-exit failure observation are removed. Other retained table scores match.

T1.justification: The driving-score definitions and other mathematical content are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal propositions, proofs, or theoretical derivations that differ between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reducing learner–expert asymmetries, mitigating target-point bias, and releasing a training stack with strong CARLA performance and sim-to-real benefits. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The long-route discussion shifts from accumulating errors and ineffective recovery to increased exposure to rare scenarios. Section 5.1 reframes off-route recovery as part of a remaining behavior-cloning gap and removes the specific limitation concerning missed highway exits. The sim-to-real qualification remains.

D1.justification: Table 5 replaces explicit camera counts with 110°, 140°, and 360° field-of-view information, and Figure 3 clarifies sensor/status token flow. The printed repository location changes from autonomousvision/lead to kesai-labs/lead. Removing the timing discussion and rewriting limitations also removes inference-hardware and viewpoint-perturbation details.

R1.justification: All 64 cited works and the central relationship to prior expert-alignment and TransFuser research are retained. However, the removed inference-time discussion withdraws the explicit efficiency advantage over SimLingo and the associated positioning of TFv6 as a practical base for future CARLA research.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites to the Learning by Cheating explanation, experiment overview, radar description, and limitations, alongside grammatical corrections and affiliation/acknowledgment updates. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the architecture diagram in Figure 3, restyles Figures 1–2, revises Table 5's camera column and several captions, and removes the inference-time table. The real-world results table is consequently renumbered from Table 7 to Table 6, with local page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 improves documentation through the architecture diagram, explicit training-seed reporting, and camera field-of-view information. However, it removes useful latency evidence and a concrete highway-exit failure disclosure. The PDFs do not explain whether the revised Town13 and infraction values are corrections or new estimates. These gains in clarity and losses of empirical and limitation detail leave the net quality change uncertain.
